newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt state offers stake in agriculture firm.
newsitem.headline: Egypt state offers stake in agriculture firm.

text.p: The state's Holding Company for Agricultural Development on Tuesday offered investors 20 percent in its Nubareya Agricultural Engineering and Mechanisation at a minimum price of 24.50 pounds per share.
The firm said in a published announcement that the public offer of at least 200,000 shares, of the firm's total one million shares, would be open to the public for two days from May 18.
The announced share price is a discovery price and can be changed upwards.
The holding company is also offering 100,000 shares or 10 percent of its stake in Nubareya to the firm's Employee Shareholders' Association.
Individuals must apply for at least 100 shares, while mutual funds and financial firms have a 1,000 share minimum.
Incentives for the new shareholders include the dividend per share for the 1996/7 financial year, which Nubareya forecast would be 2.56 pounds. The financial year ends on June 30.
Nubareya forecast net after-tax profit for 1996/7 to fall slightly to 3.5 million pounds from 3.6 million pounds in 1995/6.
Net sales are expected to shrink to 32.50 million pounds from 36.17 million in 1995/6.
National Bank of Egypt is the agent for the sale.
The share offer is part of Egypt's privatisation-led economic reform programme.
